name: write_file
description: Creates a new file or fully overwrites an existing one with the given content. Every call is autonomous and requires both 'path' and 'content' (no state is inherited from prior calls). For a large file, use resumable mode: each call must provide the same 'path', the chunk 'content', and the exact UTF-8 byte 'offset' returned by the previous call (start with offset: 0). Example: initial chunk {path: 'f.txt', content: '...', offset: 0}; intermediate chunk {path: 'f.txt', content: '...', offset: 500}; final commit chunk {path: 'f.txt', content: '...', offset: 1000, complete: true}. The destination file remains completely unchanged until complete: true is sent.

path.description: The relative or absolute path of the file to create/overwrite/append to. Required on EVERY call, including subsequent chunks of a resumable write.

content.description: The text content to write. Required on EVERY call. In resumable mode, this is the specific UTF-8 chunk for the current offset.

append.description: If true, appends 'content' to the end of the file instead of overwriting it (creates the file if it doesn't exist yet). Do not combine with resumable offset.

offset.description: Optional resumable-write offset in UTF-8 bytes. Start at 0 for the first chunk. Every later chunk must provide the exact next offset returned by the previous call. Do not combine with append.

complete.description: Only for resumable mode. Set true on the final chunk to atomically commit changes to the destination file. Until complete: true, the destination file is untouched.
